The Masoretic punctuation demands the latter translation, when the words would be an emphatic elucidation of the preceding המּה. Were they a subscription, we should expect אלּה instead of הם; while, on the other hand, the circumstance noticed by Bertheau, that in the following verses the duties not merely of the doorkeepers, but of the Levites in general, are enumerated, would seem to favour that sense. Even in the second half of the <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.22">1Ch 9:22</reference> it is not the doorkeepers who are spoken of, but the Levites in general. May we not suppose that the text originally stood היוּ הלויּם וּמן (cf. <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.14">1Ch 9:14</reference>) instead of והיוּ הויּם והם, and that the reading of our present text, having originated in a transcriber’s error, found acceptance from the circumstance that <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.27">1Ch 9:27</reference> apparently still treats of, or returns to, the service of the doorkeepers? So much is certain, that from <hi type="italic"><reference osisRef="1Chr.9.26">1Ch 9:26</reference></hi> onward the duties of the Levites in general, no longer those of the doorkeepers, are spoken of, and that consequently we must regard the Levites (הלויּם), and not the before-mentioned four doorkeepers, as the subject of והיוּ: “and the Levites were over the cells of the storehouses of the house of God.” The cells in the outbuildings of the temple served as treasure-chambers and storehouses for the temple furniture. האוצרות with the article in the stat. constr. (Ew. §290, d.), because of the looser connection, since the genitive בּית־הא also belongs to הלּשׁכוה.
entries.995320092ea8bb59801cdb92775cf68803ab16d9: <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.27">1Ch 9:27</reference> <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.27">1Ch 9:27</reference> refers again to the doorkeepers. They passed the night around the house of God, because the care of or watch over it was committed to them, and “they were over the key, and that every morning,” i.e., they had to open the door every morning. מפתּח occurs again in Jdg 3:25 and <reference osisRef="Isa.22.22">Isa 22:22</reference>, in the signification key, which is suitable here also.
entries.28fb20aaa68d95acc4556bcada85e401408d1d2c: <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.28">1Ch 9:28</reference> <div eID="gen5675" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5676" type="x-p"/> And of them (the Levites), some were over the vessels of the service, by which we are probably to understand the costly vessels, e.g., the golden cups for the libations, etc., which were brought from the treasure-chamber only for a short time for use in the service. They were brought, according to the number, into the place where the service took place, and after being again numbered, were again carried forth; and according to <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.29">1Ch 9:29</reference>, other Levites were set over הכּלים and over הקּדשׁ כּלי.
entries.71a064959e7750fa71726225a5018efc50eccd97: <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.29">1Ch 9:29</reference> <div eID="gen5676" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5677" type="x-p"/> And of them, others were set over the vessels (in general), and over all the holy vessels which were used for the daily sacrificial service, and over the fine flour (סלת,<hi type="italic">vide </hi>on <reference osisRef="Lev.2.1">Lev 2:1</reference>), wine, oil, and incense which was required therein for the meat and drink offerings, and the בּשׂמים, spicery, for the holy perfumes (frankincense, cf. <reference osisRef="Exod.25.6">Exo 25:6</reference>).
entries.60be4e491fcc29e5259dc42dbe6a7165c9ee6591: <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.30">1Ch 9:30</reference> <div eID="gen5677" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5678" type="x-p"/> And of the priests’ sons were preparers of the ointments for the spices. It is the preparation from various spices of the holy anointing oil, <reference osisRef="Exod.30.23-Exod.30.25">Exo 30:23-25</reference>, which is meant, and which consequently was part of the priest’s duty.
entries.ac7cefd1a97ff6032abb720ab716fc4e0ea6bbed: <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.31">1Ch 9:31</reference> <div eID="gen5678" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5679" type="x-p"/> Mattithiah, the first-born of the Korahite Shallum (<hi type="italic">vide</hi> <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.19">1Ch 9:19</reference>), was on good faith over the panbakings (pastry) for the meat-offerings, over the preparation of which he was to watch. To the name Mattithiah מן־הלויּם is added, in contrast to the הכּהנים מן־בּני in 1Ch 9:30. The word החבתּים (pastry, panbaking) occurs here only; cf. מחבת, pan of sheet iron, Exo 4:3.
entries.9eb575f5687086ea58137e9b6cbd6d8802874550: <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.32">1Ch 9:32</reference> <div eID="gen5679" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5680" type="x-p"/> Finally, to some of the Kohathites was committed the preparation of the shew-bread, which required to be laid on the table fresh every Sabbath; cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.24.5">Lev 24:5</reference>-8. The suffix אחיהם refers back to the Levites of the father's-house of Korah in 1Ch 9:32.
entries.06fd073c54d242cb0c02ebd0f870016a4e7ce743: <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.33-1Chr.9.34">1Ch 9:33-34</reference> <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.33">1Ch 9:33</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.34">1Ch 9:34</reference> contain subscriptions to the section vv. 14-32. Since the enumeration of the Levites dwelling in Jerusalem in <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.14-1Chr.9.16">1Ch 9:14-16</reference> began with the Levitic singer families, so here we find that the singers are mentioned in the first subscription, “these are the singers, heads of fathers'-houses of the Levites,” with an additional remark as to their service: “In the cells free, for day and night it is incumbent upon them to be in service,” which is somewhat obscure. פּטוּרים, from פּטר, in later Hebrew, let loose, set free. Rashi and Kimchi have already translated it, <hi type="italic">immunes ab aliis nempe ministeriis</hi>, or <hi type="italic">ab omni alio officio</hi>. Adopting this linguistically assured translation, we must supply with בּלּשׁכת, dwelling or waiting in the cells of the courts of the temple, freed from every other business in order that they may apply themselves wholly to their service, for they are wholly busied therewith day and night. Day and night is not to be pressed, but signifies perpetually, continually. Bertheau translates בּמּלאכה עליהם, “they were over them in the service,” i.e., had to take the oversight of the singers subordinate to them. but this can hardly be correct; and the passage quoted to justify this translation, <reference osisRef="2Chr.34.12">2Ch 34:12</reference>, proves nothing, because there מפקד is used along with it. We therefore prefer to take עליהם in the signification “it is incumbent upon them,” although we should then expect המּלאכה instead of בּמּלאכה; cf. 1Ch 9:27. Yet בּמּלאכה can in this connection quite well be used elliptically or concisely for “to be in service,” i.e., to carry on their musical duties. The second subscription (<reference osisRef="1Chr.9.34">1Ch 9:34</reference>) refers to all the Levites, and is similar in contents and form to that in 1Ch 8:28.
entries.9413b3fad27cce01cf9899d995b12f9ec876feee: <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.35-1Chr.9.44">1Ch 9:35-44</reference> <hi type="italic">The family of King Saul</hi>. - This register has already occurred in <reference osisRef="1Chr.8.29-1Chr.8.38">1Ch 8:29-38</reference>, along with those of other families of the tribe of Benjamin, and is repeated here only to connect the following history of the kingship with the preceding genealogical lists. It forms here the introduction to the narrative of Saul’s death in <reference osisRef="1Chr.10.1-1Chr.10.14">1Ch 10:1-14</reference>, which in turn forms the transition to the kingship of David. The deviations of this register from that in <reference osisRef="1Chr.8.29-1Chr.8.38">1Ch 8:29-38</reference>, show that it has been derived from another document in more complete preservation than that in 1 Chron 8, which had been handed down in connection with other genealogies of the Benjamite families, and had suffered considerably in its text. See the commentary on <reference osisRef="1Chr.8.29">1Ch 8:29</reference>-38.  <chapter eID="1Chr.9"/> <div eID="gen5680" type="x-p"/>

                  <ns0:p n="1">1 SO all Israel were reckoned by genealogies: and behold, they <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> written in the book of the Kings of Israel and Judah <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Not in that Sacred and Canonical Book so called, but (as hath been oft observed before) in the Publick Records, wherein there was an Account of that King and Kingdom, and of the several Fami<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lies in it according to their Genealogies.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>who</ns0:hi>

                  <ns0:p n="4">4 Uthai, the son of Ammihud <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">That there is so great a diversity of Names between this Cata<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />logue and that <ns0:hi>Nehem.</ns0:hi> 11. may be ascribed to two causes, first to the Custom of the Hebrews who used very frequently to give 2. or 3. several Names to one person: And secondly to the change of Times; for here they are named who came up at the first Return; but many of those in <ns0:hi>Nehemiah</ns0:hi> might be such as returned after<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward and came and dwelt either in stead of the Persons here named, who might be then dead or gone from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> or with them.</ns0:note>, the son of Omri the son of Imri, the son of B<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
